standard_prerequisites: Dependent pair types with their projections and dependent function types.
The uniqueness principle for dependent pair types (the retained context).
Function extensionality: pointwise identified dependent functions are identified.
The uniqueness principle for functions applied to the pair of pointwise parts.
core_obligations: Construct the quasi-inverse sending a pair (g, h) with g a section of A and h a section of the fibre family over g to the function x maps to the pair (g(x), h(x)).

Prove the first round-trip: the pointwise pairing of the projections of a section f is pointwise identified with f by the Sigma uniqueness principle, hence identified as dependent functions by function extensionality.
Prove the second round-trip: the pointwise projections of the pairing of (g, h) are judgmentally the pair (g, h).
Conclude that the projection map is an equivalence.
proof_roadmap: Define the inverse: send (g, h) to the dependent function x maps to (g(x), h(x)), exactly as in the non-dependent case.

First direction: the round-trip on a section f yields the function x maps to the pair of projections of f(x); by the Sigma uniqueness principle (the retained context) each instance is identified with f(x); by function extensionality the dependent functions are identified.
Second direction: the round-trip on (g, h) yields the pair of pointwise parts, judgmentally equal to (g, h) as before.
Conclude the equivalence; the author remarks that under the propositions-as-types reading this statement is the type-theoretic axiom of choice.
difficulty_reason: Structurally parallel to the product universal property but dependent throughout; the round-trip uses the Sigma uniqueness principle pointwise plus function extensionality, and the bookkeeping must respect the dependency.
